# Results — Study 739 (Wildfire-Season)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test:
**California's fire season is a repeating, tradable risk event for the state's
utilities and property insurers** — a major wildfire should hammer the exposed basket
(Edison / `EIX`, PG&E / `PCG`, and CA-property insurers `ALL`/`TRV`/`MCY`/`CB`) on the
news, and the whole July→December fire window should carry a systematically worse
basket return than the rest of the calendar. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`62b4a2a1757b` (EIX) / `759d993391f0` (PCG) / `7898cdc31849` (ALL) / `3a070b43af0e`
(TRV) / `c95d75857b2a` (MCY) / `36b3badbd526` (CB) / `1ecb87f843e4` (SPY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), 5,910 rows each, 2003-01-02 → 2026-06-30, for EIX, PCG, ALL, TRV, MCY, CB and SPY. Every ticker has continuous history over the sample, so basket coverage is full on every event date |
| Fire calendar | **hardcoded** table of **14 major California wildfire events** 2003-10-25 → 2025-01-07 (front-page, billion-dollar fires). Each row flags `utility_linked` — whether an investor-owned utility's equipment was the confirmed/leading-suspected ignition cause. **7 utility-linked** (Witch/Oct-2007, Oct-2017/Tubbs, Thomas, Camp+Woolsey, Kincade, Dixie, Eaton+Palisades), **7 non-utility** (Cedar, Rim, Valley, Carr, Aug-2020 lightning siege, Creek, Mosquito). Same-market-day co-ignitions merged (Camp+Woolsey 2018-11-08; Eaton+Palisades 2025-01-07) |
| Baskets | combined (all 6), utility leg (EIX/PCG), insurer leg (ALL/TRV/MCY/CB) — equal-weight, daily-rebalanced |
| Statistics | One-sample *t* across the 14 independent, non-overlapping event dates (for the ignition-day return, the [+1..+5] window and the paired differences); Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebo; leave-one-out jackknife and event bootstrap for outlier sensitivity; a random-6-month-window placebo for the seasonal |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the fire's ignition date is snapped to the first NYSE session on/after it (weekday ignitions land same-day, weekend ignitions roll to the next open) — zero look-ahead, since the ignition is public before that session's close. The timer **shorts** the basket at that session's close, exits `hold` sessions later; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; the short pays a 300 bps/yr borrow fee prorated over the hold |
| Survivorship | **PG&E's 2019 Chapter 11 and dilution are *inside* the total-return `PCG` tape**, not survivored out — a real shareholder lived through them. No cross-sectional membership panel is used, so no opt-in survivorship guard applies |

## The headline — combined-basket ignition-day (day 0) abnormal return

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean ignition-day abnormal basket return | **−22.77 bps** |
| one-sample *t* (n=14) | **−0.92** |
| hit rate (basket down on the day) | **9/14 = 64.3%** (Wilson 95% [38.8%, 83.7%]) |

On the day a major California wildfire breaks out, the exposed basket moves an
**indistinguishable-from-zero −22.77 bps** — the sign is right but *t* is under one and
the hit rate's Wilson interval spans a coin flip. **Random-calendar placebo:** observed
−22.77 bps vs placebo mean −0.31 bps (sd 36.04 bps) over **20,000 draws (20 seeds ×
1,000)** → **left-tail p = 0.242**. A random calendar of 14 days produces a dip this
size about a quarter of the time. **There is no same-day "fire flinch."**

## Event window — mean abnormal basket return by offset [−1..+5]

| offset | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean (bps) | −57.05 | **−22.77** | −74.35 | **−149.74** | −66.23 | −7.84 | +33.22 |
| CAR (bps) | +0.00 | **−22.77** | −97.11 | −246.86 | −313.09 | −320.92 | −287.71 |
| *t* | **−2.17** | **−0.92** | −1.38 | −1.70 | −1.18 | −0.11 | +0.51 |

The drift is negative for the first several sessions — the drop *builds* over the days
**after** ignition, exactly as you'd expect if it's the *liability* (who-caused-it)
news landing, not a same-day sentiment flinch. But no post-ignition offset clears the
|*t*| ≥ 2 desk bar. The one bar that does — offset **−1** (*t* = −2.17) — is on the
**wrong side of the event** (the day *before* the fire is public), a textbook
look-elsewhere false positive among 7 offsets, with no mechanism.

## The liability window — cumulative abnormal return [+1..+5]

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| combined-basket mean [+1..+5] CAR | **−264.94 bps** |
| one-sample *t* (n=14) | **−1.41** |
| event bootstrap 95% CI on the mean | **[−657.7, +41.4] bps** |
| leave-one-out \|*t*\| range | **[−1.61, −0.98]** (\|*t*\| < 2 in **14/14** drops) |

The average basket gives up **−2.6%** over the five sessions after a fire — a real,
economically large number, but the bootstrap CI **crosses zero** and *every* single
leave-one-out drop keeps |*t*| under 2. The effect is **not** statistically robust;
it hangs on a handful of megafires.

## Utility leg vs insurer leg ([+1..+5] window)

| leg | mean [+1..+5] CAR | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| utility (EIX/PCG) | **−704.11 bps** | **−1.51** |
| insurer (ALL/TRV/MCY/CB) | −45.35 bps | −0.60 |
| paired (utility − insurer) | **−658.76 bps** | −1.54 |

**The utilities carry essentially all of it.** The utility leg drops **−7.0%** over the
week after a fire; the insurer leg is flat (−0.45%). Property insurers — the names the
folklore says are "on the hook for the claims" — barely twitch: they are diversified,
reinsured, nationally spread, and a single state's fire loss is a footnote to their
book. The whole story, such as it is, lives in the two utilities' **inverse-condemnation
liability** — a fundamental repricing of "did our equipment start this", not a
sentiment or calendar effect.

## Utility-linked subset — utility leg, fires an IOU's equipment (likely) started

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n (utility-linked fires) | **7** |
| ignition-day (day 0) | **−22.27 bps** (*t* = **−0.47**) |
| [+1..+5] CAR | **−1596.35 bps** (*t* = **−1.96**) |
| leave-one-out \|*t*\| < 2 | in **5/7** drops |

Restrict to the 7 fires a utility's equipment (likely) started and the utility leg
gives up **−16%** over the following week (*t* = −1.96 — one hair short of the bar) —
while the ignition day *itself* is still flat (*t* = −0.47). This is the honest core
of the study: **the drop is real, it is a delayed fundamental repricing of liability,
and it is fragile** — 5 of 7 leave-one-out draws push |*t*| below 2, i.e. it hinges on
Camp (PG&E, −63% in five sessions) and Eaton (Edison, −21%). Take out one megafire and
the "signal" evaporates.

## Extra drop vs the market — does the CA basket fall harder than SPY? ([+1..+5])

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| basket [+1..+5] CAR | −264.94 bps |
| SPY [+1..+5] CAR | +24.86 bps |
| paired (basket − SPY) difference | **−289.80 bps** (*t* = **−1.71**, n=14) |

The CA-exposed basket does underperform the market by ~2.9% over the post-fire week,
same direction the claim predicts — but again under the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar and, per the leg
split above, entirely a utility-liability story.

## The seasonal half — Jul→Dec fire window vs the rest of the year

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| fire-window mean (n=2,928 days) | **+1.809 bps/day** |
| rest-of-year mean (n=2,981 days) | **−1.777 bps/day** |
| gap (in − out) | **+3.586 bps/day** |
| Welch *t* | **+1.019** |
| random-6-month-window two-sided *p* | **0.297** |

The "sell in July for California risk" seasonal is **not there — and it points the
wrong way.** The basket's abnormal return is if anything marginally *higher* inside the
July→December fire window (utilities are defensive, dividend-heavy names that tend to do
*well* in autumn risk-off), the Welch *t* is +1.0, and a random 6-month slice of the
calendar produces a gap this big about 30% of the time. **Busted.**

## The timer — short the basket on the ignition headline

*The folklore trade: fires are bad news for the basket, so you **short** it.* Enter the
basket short at the ignition-session close (zero look-ahead), hold `hold` sessions; one
round trip of 5 bps one-way charged twice, plus 300 bps/yr borrow prorated over the
hold.

| hold | gross mean | gross **median** | net mean | *t* (net) | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 days | +227.91 bps | **+30.90 bps** | +211.96 bps | +1.19 | 57% |
| 10 days | +197.69 bps | +141.15 bps | +175.79 bps | +1.16 | 57% |
| 21 days | +116.92 bps | +11.37 bps | +81.92 bps | +0.45 | 43% |

The mean short return is positive, but it is a **lottery, not an edge.** At the 5-day
hold the *mean* is +228 bps while the *median* is +31 bps — the average is carried by
two PG&E/Edison bankruptcy-scale jackpots (Camp, Eaton) inside 14 bets. It never clears
*t* ≥ 2 net of borrow, the win rate is barely above a coin flip, and by 21 days it has
decayed to +82 bps with a **43%** win rate (you lose more often than you win). You are
paying borrow to short a basket of defensive dividend stocks on the off-chance a given
fire turns out to be utility-caused — a negative-carry bet on a rare jackpot.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic random-walk tape with 14 scheduled "fire" dates and a TUNABLE planted
day-0 dip that reverts over the next 5 sessions; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (dip = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.09** (sd 0.96), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (the nominal 5% rate) |
| planted dip = −3.0% (seed 739) | **−10.92** |

The detector sits at the nominal false-positive rate on the null (1 in 20 ≈ 5%) and
lights up sharply on a planted dip. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The ignition day is flat (combined basket **−22.77 bps**,
  *t* = **−0.92**, hit rate 64.3% [Wilson 38.8–83.7%], random-calendar placebo
  **p = 0.242**). The real craters arrive in the days *after* ignition as liability is
  assigned, but the [+1..+5] window doesn't clear the bar either (basket *t* = −1.41,
  bootstrap CI crosses zero, 14/14 leave-one-out below 2); the best cut — the utility
  leg on the 7 utility-linked fires — reaches only *t* = −1.96 and is fragile (5/7
  leave-one-out below 2, Camp/Eaton-driven). Insurers essentially don't react
  (*t* = −0.60). Nothing clears a robust |*t*| ≥ 2.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Shorting the basket on the fire headline has a positive
  mean but a tiny median — a 2-jackpot lottery, never significant net of borrow
  (best *t* = +1.19), decaying to a 43% win rate by 21 days. There is no systematic,
  costable edge; there is a rare, un-timeable liability crater.
- **"A sell-in-July fire-season seasonal?" — BUSTED.** The July→December window is
  marginally *positive* for the basket (wrong sign, Welch *t* = +1.0, random-window
  *p* = 0.30). The calendar does not price California fire risk in advance.

The intuitive truth ("PG&E's fire destroyed the stock") is real — but it is a
**fundamental, delayed, utility-specific liability repricing concentrated in two
megafires**, not the same-day, basket-wide, seasonal, tradable pattern the folklore
describes.
